chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Dorothy Dandridge and the "Pillar to Post" soundtrack
summary: Dandridge sang once with Armstrong in the film, whose trick arrangements had to be simplified in the recording studio.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I see. And you were with Louie now for about a year?
About a year, yeah. A year or year and a half.
Up to about 1945.
1945, yeah.
Okay. I want to back up a second on a couple of things.
Oh, I see that Dorothy Dandridge was a vocalist with that Armstrong band, at least for a while while you were with him. Do you remember her being in there?
That was a -- She was a movie star, right?
Yeah.
She was in California.
She was in Carmen Jones and a couple of other films.
When we went out to California, she just sang with us once. And she sang in

the picture, Pillar To The Post.
I see.
It was a big cabaret scene. I think I remember telling you about when we went there, Falstein (inaudible), that's the first time I met him -- Warner Brothers.
Okay.
I met him and he was directing and Dorothy was doing the vocal with Louie in the picture.
And we had a lot of trouble, because I arranged it -- we call ourselves doing something different, you know.
Like we used to write for Ella, you know. The band would hit a chord, Ella would hit up one chord and we would dissolve it away from her, you know.
It be like an off thing, you know, and she would go -- the vocal will go one way and the band would be moving away from her, and then all come back together again.
Well, Dorothy didn't have that type of

We did the -- in fact, we did the music to the -- everything we was gonna do in the picture, we recorded that before --
The soundtrack.
Before we went in to do he picture. Worked from the soundtrack.
